patient_selection.evidence: Parameters for imaging the test object and normal human volunteers were set to values that decreased the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), caused distortion, and increased the slice thickness and separation.
patient_selection.rationale: Abstract only; volunteers and a test object are mentioned but no sampling rule, number of subjects, or inclusion/exclusion criteria are described.

index_test.evidence: To evaluate the validity of this assumption, we compared the sensitivity of a test object and automated image analysis system for MR imaging QC with the sensitivity of trained human observers
index_test.rationale: No statement about whether observers were blinded to which images had been degraded or to the degradation level, and no pre-specified detection threshold is reported.

reference_standard.evidence: with the sensitivity of trained human observers by evaluating images that were intentionally degraded
reference_standard.rationale: The ground truth was the experimentally applied degradation, which is known by construction and therefore classifies the target condition (presence/level of degradation) correctly.

flow_timing.rationale: The abstract gives no information on how many images or observers entered the analysis, or whether any data were excluded.

app_patient_selection.evidence: Parameters for imaging the test object and normal human volunteers were set to values that decreased the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), caused distortion, and increased the slice thickness and separation.
app_patient_selection.rationale: A phantom test object plus normal volunteers, with no clinical brain-MRI patient population, does not match a review question about preserving diagnostic content in patients.

app_index_test.evidence: Automated analysis of test object images was able to detect all image degradations at the minimum levels applied.
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is deliberate parameter-driven degradation assessed by an automated QC system, not an accelerated or AI-based image reconstruction.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Further investigation is needed to better define the accuracy with which quantitative image-quality analysis predicts the effects of degraded image quality on the ability of human observers to detect subtle abnormalities in clinical images.
app_reference_standard.rationale: The authors explicitly state that the link between image-quality degradation and detection of clinical abnormalities was not established, so the reference does not address diagnostic content.

patient_selection.evidence: We measured human and channelized Hotelling observers in a two-alternative forced-choice signal-known-exactly detection task on synthetic MR images.
patient_selection.rationale: No patients were sampled at all; the material is synthetic imagery with inserted signals, an artificial signal-present/signal-absent design analogous to case-control selection.

index_test.evidence: We compared three reconstructions: magnitude, wavelet-based denoising, and phase-corrected real. Human observers performed approximately equally using all three reconstructions.
index_test.rationale: Three reconstructions were compared but the abstract does not say whether observers were blinded to which reconstruction they were viewing (only full text available is a mismatched PDF of an unrelated sonar paper).

reference_standard.evidence: We measured human and channelized Hotelling observers in a two-alternative forced-choice signal-known-exactly detection task on synthetic MR images.
reference_standard.rationale: Signal-known-exactly truth on synthetic images means the reference is correct by construction and independent of the observers' decisions.

flow_timing.rationale: No information on the number of trials, observers, or images entering the analysis, or on any exclusions.

app_patient_selection.evidence: We measured human and channelized Hotelling observers in a two-alternative forced-choice signal-known-exactly detection task on synthetic MR images.
app_patient_selection.rationale: Synthetic images with no human subjects and no stated anatomy do not match a review question about brain MRI in patients.

app_index_test.evidence: We compared three reconstructions: magnitude, wavelet-based denoising, and phase-corrected real. Human observers performed approximately equally using all three reconstructions.
app_index_test.rationale: The reconstructions compared are magnitude/denoising/phase-correction for low-SNR images rather than accelerated or undersampled brain reconstruction.

app_reference_standard.evidence: We measured human and channelized Hotelling observers in a two-alternative forced-choice signal-known-exactly detection task on synthetic MR images.
app_reference_standard.rationale: The ground truth is an inserted synthetic signal, not a fully sampled acquisition or an expert radiological reading of real pathology.

patient_selection.evidence: Three high resolution raw parallel MRI brain data sets (T2-weighted, flip angle = 90°, TR/TE = 3000/85 ms, matrix size 512×512, slice thickness = 20mm, FOV = 205mm×205mm, resolution 0.4mm×0.4mm) were acquired from a healthy volunteer.
patient_selection.rationale: The entire image material comes from three planes of a single healthy volunteer, a convenience sample with no selection rule and no patients.

index_test.evidence: Observers were aware that we considered the reference image to be “best” and that they should consider it to have a score of zero
index_test.rationale: Observers were explicitly told which panel was the fully sampled reference and which was the reconstructed test image, so ratings of the index reconstruction were made unblinded.

reference_standard.evidence: Each human subject presentation consisted of a two-panel display, with the high-quality reference image and a randomly selected test image on the left and right, respectively.
reference_standard.rationale: The fully sampled reference was displayed simultaneously in a fixed, identified position, so it was not interpreted independently of the index test.

flow_timing.evidence: Data for CS reconstruction was generated synthetically by randomly under-sampling the two-dimensional reference k-space data, which was obtained from the reference image through Fourier transform, in the phase encoding direction.
flow_timing.rationale: All test reconstructions were derived retrospectively from the same reference k-space, so the interval is zero and every test image shares an identical reference standard.

app_patient_selection.evidence: As the current study did not include pathological data, we will continue to study the performance of Artifact-PDM for evaluation of clinical images.
app_patient_selection.rationale: The authors concede that no pathological or clinical data were included, so the sample cannot speak to preservation of diagnostic content in patients.

app_index_test.evidence: A Total Variation (TV) and Wavelet Transform (WT) sparsification based CS reconstruction algorithm15, and the GRAPPA parallel MRI k-space reconstruction algorithm27 were evaluated and compared in this paper.
app_index_test.rationale: Compressed sensing and GRAPPA accelerated reconstructions of brain data are exactly the class of index test the review addresses.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Four engineers and one radiologist, aged between 19 and 33 years, participated in the FMT (Eng_1-4 and Rad) and DSCQS (Eng_1-2) experiments as observers.
app_reference_standard.rationale: Ground truth is perceptual quality/artifact-disturbance rating by a panel that is mostly engineers, not a diagnostic reading, so it does not index diagnostic content.

patient_selection.evidence: SWI data from 28 traumatic brain injury (TBI) patients was obtained on a 3 tesla clinical Siemens scanner using both the product 3D gradient echo sequence (GRE) with generalized autocalibrating partially parallel acquisition acceleration
patient_selection.rationale: A single-centre series of 28 referred TBI patients with no statement that enrolment was consecutive or random and no inclusion/exclusion criteria given.

index_test.evidence: for the presence or absence of punctate foci of signal loss on the magnitude images, SWI images, and correlated with the presence of singularities at the free ends of OEFs
index_test.rationale: A single unblinded reader, who is also a study author, scored the accelerated SWI images while explicitly correlating findings with the phase-singularity locations used to define the artifact.

reference_standard.evidence: Another limitation is the indirect characterization of the artifactual microhemorrhage. This study relied on comparing phase data using two different methods, i.e. sEPI and GRAPPA-accelerated GRE for obtaining phase data which should be very close.
reference_standard.rationale: The authors themselves describe the reference as indirect; absence of a lesion on magnitude/sEPI images is assumed to prove artifact, and the same unblinded reader judged both arms.

flow_timing.evidence: To generate SWI, magnitude and phase images were obtained using both 3D GRE and 3D in-house developed sEPI methods (18) in each patient. Geometric parameters were identical for both sequences
flow_timing.rationale: Every patient received both the index and comparator acquisitions in the same session with matched geometry, and all 28 cases are accounted for in the results.

app_patient_selection.evidence: Review of the 28 TBI cases acquired from the Siemens scanner showed that type III OEFs were present in 19 (68%) phase datasets obtained using GRAPPA-accelerated GRE
app_patient_selection.rationale: Real clinical brain MRI in TBI patients, the population in which accelerated SWI reconstruction safety actually matters.

app_index_test.evidence: Acceleration was achieved using GRAPPA×2 for the single echo GRE and an echo train length of 15 for the EPI without GRAPPA.
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is a GRAPPA-accelerated acquisition with vendor SWI reconstruction, directly on point for whether accelerated reconstruction can create false diagnostic findings.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Because the comparable GRE sequence without GRAPPA was prohibitively long (~20 minutes), we were unable to obtain phase information from the identical sequence without GRAPPA.
app_reference_standard.rationale: No fully sampled version of the same sequence was available; the comparator is a different in-house research sequence rather than a fully sampled or standard-of-care acquisition.

patient_selection.evidence: In total, 192, 88, 76 and 55 brain images are acquired using T2*, T1, T2 and contrast-enhanced T1 (T1C) weighted MR imaging sequences, respectively.
patient_selection.rationale: Image counts are given but the number of participants, the recruitment period and any consecutive or random sampling rule are not stated; healthy-brain and brain-tumour scans come from different sources.

index_test.evidence: To each imaging protocol, the consistency of SNR measurement is verified between and within two observers, and white matter (WM) and cerebral spinal fluid (CSF) are alternately used as the tissue region of interest (TOI) for SNR measurement.
index_test.rationale: The two observers (a non-physician and a radiologist) delineated regions separately and independently, and the reliability and correlation interpretation thresholds (ICC and Pearson bands) were pre-specified.

reference_standard.evidence: Comparatively, no-reference MIQA algorithms are more useful and challenging, and no reference information can be borrowed [20, 23, 26].
reference_standard.rationale: There is no fully sampled reference image and no expert diagnostic reading; observer-measured SNR itself serves as the standard, which cannot establish correct classification of diagnostic quality.

flow_timing.evidence: The procedure is repeated on another day within 30 days.
flow_timing.rationale: Identical measurement procedure applied to all images by both observers at both time points, with all sequences reported in the results tables and no exclusions described.

app_patient_selection.evidence: in this study, 411 in vivo human brain MR images are collected and 2 observers are involved to localize the tissue regions of white matter (WM)
app_patient_selection.rationale: In vivo human brain MR images across four clinical sequences, including tumour patients, is an applicable population for a brain MRI image-quality question.

app_index_test.evidence: four models (BIQI, BLIINDS-II, BRISQUE and NIQE) primarily used for the quality assessment of natural images are borrowed to predict the quality of MR images
app_index_test.rationale: No accelerated, compressed-sensing or deep-learning reconstruction is evaluated; the index measures are SNR and no-reference natural-image quality models.

app_reference_standard.evidence: When SNR measurement performs as the quality indicator of MR images, BRISQUE and BLIINDS-II can be conditionally used for the automated quality estimation of human brain MR images.
app_reference_standard.rationale: SNR is used as the quality standard in place of a fully sampled acquisition or radiologist reading, so the study cannot speak to preservation of diagnostic content.

patient_selection.evidence: A total number of 56 patients with dizziness (33 males and 23 females; mean age, 53.4 ± 18.6 years) were enrolled in this study between March 2017 and July 2017.
patient_selection.rationale: Prospective enrolment over a defined period at one centre, but the report does not state that patients were consecutive or randomly selected, nor give inclusion/exclusion criteria.

index_test.evidence: by two neuroradiologists (with 5 and 26 years of experience) who were blinded to the acquisition parameters and patients’ information
index_test.rationale: Readers were blinded to acquisition parameters (hence to acceleration factor) and used detailed, pre-specified five-point grading scales.

reference_standard.evidence: Afterward, sparse TOF images acquired with net acceleration factors of 3.5 and 5 were compared with conventional TOF images acquired using GRAPPA acceleration factors of 2 and 3, respectively.
reference_standard.rationale: The comparator is the conventional standard-of-care TOF protocol, scored by the same two readers under the same blinding, so the standard was applied independently of acceleration status.

flow_timing.evidence: The acquisition and image reconstruction were successful for all 56 patients. Among them, five were diagnosed as having vessel stenoses, while the others presented healthy intracranial vasculatures.
flow_timing.rationale: Both sequences were acquired in the same session in every patient and all 56 patients were included in the analysis with no dropouts.

app_patient_selection.evidence: Second, the subjects in this study were mostly patients without lesions in vessels; thus, diagnostic accuracies were not compared in the current study.
app_patient_selection.rationale: Only 5 of 56 patients had vascular pathology, so the spectrum is too normal to demonstrate that acceleration preserves diagnostic content.

app_index_test.evidence: For the sparse TOF prototype sequence, each slab was acquired using a variable-density Poisson disk sampling pattern in the ky - kz phase-encoding plane (17-22) with acceleration factors of 3.5 and 5.
app_index_test.rationale: Sparse undersampling with inline iterative reconstruction at acceleration factors of 3.5 and 5 in brain MRA is precisely the index test of interest.

app_reference_standard.evidence: The image quality was scored using a five-point scale based on the delineation of arterial vessel segments, artifacts, overall vessel visualization, and overall image quality by two radiologists independently
app_reference_standard.rationale: Conventional TOF read independently by two neuroradiologists using diagnosis-anchored quality scales matches the review's reference standard, although the comparator is itself GRAPPA-accelerated.
